title: Install or recover Iatreion
summary: Install, inspect, or recover Iatreion programs and their provider selector. Installation performs setup and basic execution checks.
use_when: Iatreion programs should be installed, inspected, or recovered.
do_not_use_when: Only an operational report is needed.
outcome: The supplied programs and provider are selected together, or an explicit setup failure.
effects: Copy supplied programs and documentation into retained releases and select owned public paths atomically. Preserve other product selectors and separate product data.
authority: Iatreion owns its program installation and provider selector. The operator supplies artifacts and authorizes selection.
success: Owned command and provider selectors follow the installed release. Basic help/version invocations complete. No artifact-integrity, persistent-state, or operational-readiness gate is run.
failure_and_recovery: Refuse foreign public selectors or stale expected-current selections. File-operation or basic execution failures restore prior selectors when possible. Recovery selects retained program files and leaves product data unchanged.
privacy: Installation retains executable and documentation bytes. It retains no report, product state, or credential.
steps: Select the intended supplied binary and provider paths and the installation home.
Read the current selection and run install with any intended expected-current guard.
Register the installed command inventory separately and read installation metadata.
Recover a retained release when requested; keep diagnostics separate from installation.
checkpoints: Owned selectors select the supplied program and provider release.
Setup and basic execution have completed. Program selection does not establish artifact integrity or live readiness.
adaptation: Use absolute paths and an intentional alternate home when required.
stop_when: Required files cannot be copied, a selector is foreign, the expected selection changed, or a required setup operation fails.

interfaces.label: Install
interfaces.invocation: iatreion-install install --binary ABS --bundle ABS [--home ABS] [--expected-current absent|releases/ID]

does_not_authorize: Release publication, deployment of product probes, or product operation.

consumers.statement: The current operator may install or recover Iatreion.

preconditions.statement: Supplied program and provider paths, an intended installation home, and authority to change owned selectors. Installation does not require a validation receipt.

inputs.statement: Absolute binary and bundle paths, optional home and expected-current selection, or one retained release path for recovery.

outputs.statement: Recorded release metadata and selected public paths, or an installation error. Inspection reports metadata without checking artifact integrity.

data_semantics.statement: Program selection is installation state. It establishes neither database integrity nor dependency readiness nor domain success.

identity_and_units.statement: Opaque UUID release IDs name staged files. Product releases, provider contract versions, and application state versions remain distinct. Installation does not compare component versions or artifact hashes.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Inspection reads current selectors and recorded installation metadata. It does not audit retained content or probe a live dependency.

access.statement: Current-user local filesystem access is bounded to Iatreion-owned release and selector paths.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Product and catalog locks serialize atomic publication. Expected-current guards detect changed selection. File-operation or basic execution failures restore the prior selection when possible. Recovery reads retained metadata without integrity validation and preserves separate product state.

operational_limits.statement: Installation copies files and performs required setup plus basic help/version execution checks. It runs no installer verify command, database integrity check, provider validation, or readiness probe. Explicit ordinary diagnostic commands keep their existing behavior.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: The installer retains its existing release layout and supported legacy metadata readers. Installer verify and verify-release commands are removed. Program recovery does not restore product data.

reliances.statement: The product-owned installer links the shared installation library and invokes no represented capability.
